CADCraft web design system

Foundations

  • Colors (.md): One base colour at an alpha ladder over a few near-black surfaces in dark, mirrored in light: colour is a signal, never decoration.
  • Icons (.md): Every icon is drawn in code as an SVG path on a 24×24 grid and takes its colour from the surrounding ink (currentColor); no icon font, sp...
  • Motion (.md): Four durations and two easings, plus the one fade endpoint for hover: motion is fast, short and never decorative — it confirms a state ch...
  • Radius (.md): The corner ladder (2–5px for controls, 20px for floating surfaces, full round for pills), the one hairline width, the focus ring's stroke...
  • Spacing (.md): One gap scale in even steps and one control-height ladder: every inset, gap and control size in the chrome is a token from these two ladd...
  • Typography (.md): Two families (the system UI stack and the mono stack) and six fixed sizes, one per control and one per reading role: text never takes a s...

Components

  • Button (.md): It runs one action the moment its label says so: it never navigates and never holds a value.
  • Chip (.md): It shows one compact fact, a keyword or a suggestion, and it only acts when the caller gives it a handler.
  • Field (.md): It takes one line of text and hands every keystroke back to the caller, who owns the value.
  • IconButton (.md): It runs one action drawn as a single glyph, and its tooltip is its accessible name.
  • Row (.md): It is the full-width clickable band of a list: a menu item, a property row or a layer, marked current when it is the selected one.
  • SectionLabel (.md): It names a panel's section as a real heading, so a screen reader can jump between the sections by heading.

Rules

  • Rules (.md): every trap and rule ID, the page that answers it and the check that enforces it

Other

  • The web system's design decisions (.md): The lock for the SolidJS UI (apps/ui), taken in the design-system run of 2026-10-28.

Check command: cd apps/ui && bun run check. Machine index: llms.txt.

Colors

Description

One base colour at an alpha ladder over a few near-black surfaces in dark, mirrored in light: colour is a signal, never decoration. This page is the token list, the role of each token, and the measured contrast of every pair; the values themselves live in src/tokens.css (measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22, the run's research notes).

Tokens

Dark is the default (:root); light restates only the roles that change, under :root[data-theme="light"], and inherits the rest.

Each specimen is drawn with the token itself, never a copied value.

  • On accent: <span style="background:var(--accent);color:var(--on-accent);padding:2px 10px">Primary</span> <span style="background:var(--error);color:var(--on-accent);padding:2px 10px">Danger</span>.

  • State fills over --control: <span style="background:var(--control);padding:2px 10px">rest <span style="background:var(--hover);padding:1px 6px">hover</span> <span style="background:var(--fill-active);padding:1px 6px">active</span> <span style="background:var(--fill-pressed);padding:1px 6px">pressed</span> <span style="background:var(--fill-disabled);padding:1px 6px">disabled</span></span>.

Usage

  • Reach for a role, never a hue: --accent for the one action, --error for a failure, --warn for a caution, --snap for a snap indicator, because a second meaning per hue makes the interface unreadable at a glance.
  • Hover and selection are fills, not colour changes — --hover, --fill-active, --fill-pressed over whatever surface the control sits on — because a hue swap changes a control's meaning, while a fill step only moves it.
  • Disabled is a lighter ink (--text-disabled) on an unchanged fill (--fill-disabled), because a disabled control should read as unavailable, not as a different control.
  • On an accent fill the label is --on-accent, never --text, because the fill is the same in both themes' buttons and the ink must stay readable on it.
  • The drawing area keeps its own colours (--canvas, --grid-*, --axis-*) in both themes, because a drawing's paper should not change when the chrome's theme does.
  • --text-faint is the lowest ink a reader must still read; anything quieter is --text-disabled, which only disabled controls carry, because an enabled control a reader cannot read is a bug, not a hierarchy.

Accessibility

Contrast, measured by node scripts/contrast-report.mjs (run from the app folder), WCAG 2.x. Every cell is the foreground composited over that surface: ratio, then ✓ at the token's threshold (4.5:1 text, 3:1 icons and borders), ✗ below it, · for the fills, which carry no threshold — their cell shows how visible the step is against the surface.

Not tokens

  • The wasm canvas draws its primitives' colours from the tokens through src/canvas.ts; its fallback literals (#181818, #202020, …) only apply when a token is missing, and the palette it reads is the token list above.
  • The axis-x/axis-y hues and the layer glyph colours are fixed in both themes on purpose: they identify canvas objects, not chrome roles.

Icons

Description

Every icon is drawn in code as an SVG path on a 24×24 grid and takes its colour from the surrounding ink (currentColor); no icon font, sprite or third-party artwork ships. The paths live in src/icons.ts, the sizes and inks in src/tokens.css.

GroupIds

Outputplot, publish, pagesetup, preview, import, export, attach, share

Toolsdist, list, area
Composersend, stop, plus, close

Usage

  • A glyph is currentColor; its container sets the ink (--icon, --icon-accent, --icon-point), because an icon must follow the state its control is in.
  • Three sizes only (12/14/16), matched to the control ladder, because a fourth size is a different control.
  • Icons are drawn, never imported: every path is original code on the 24×24 grid, because third-party icon sets carry licences and a foreign stroke grammar.
  • A glyph that means the same thing keeps its id everywhere (save is the floppy, zoom.extents the four corners), because two drawings for one action is a bug a reader reads as two actions.
  • Status glyphs keep their fixed layer colours (--icon-layer-*, --icon-current) in both themes, because a layer's state must survive the chrome's theme.

Accessibility

  • Icons are never the only label: an icon-only control carries aria-label in its component (src/ui/IconButton.tsx), and the check cannot see the rendered accessibility tree, so the browser review covers it.
  • Contrast: --icon measures 7.5:1 over --chrome in dark and 5.8:1 in light; the layer inks are exempt as state markers on the canvas. The Colors page carries the full measured grid from scripts/contrast-report.mjs.
  • The 1.5 stroke on the 24×24 grid keeps a glyph readable down to 12px without hinting.

Not tokens

  • The 24×24 viewBox and stroke-width: 1.5 are drawing constants in src/icons.ts, not tokens, because they are the glyphs' own geometry rather than chrome scale.
  • The composer's COMPOSER_ICONS list (send, stop, plus, close) is a subset marker for that pane, not a second icon set.

Motion

Description

Four durations and two easings, plus the one fade endpoint for hover: motion is fast, short and never decorative — it confirms a state change and gets out of the way. The values live in src/tokens.css, measured from Cursor 3.27.22 (durations 50/100/150/200ms, ease-out and a strong out-quint).

Tokens

TokenValueRole
--dur-instant0.05sA state that must feel immediate: the hover fill.
--dur-fast0.1sThe default: a control's fill, a border colour change.
--dur-med0.15sA panel or a popover appearing.
--dur-slow0.2sThe largest move the chrome makes (a dialog, the assistant panel).
--ease-outcubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)The default easing: fast out, settled at the end.
--ease-out-quintcubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)A stronger deceleration for the larger moves (a panel sliding in).
--hover-opacity0.8The hover fade's endpoint for quiet ink (a model chip's label).

Specimens

Each preset, drawn with its token (hover or focus the bars to replay):

  • <span style="display:inline-block;padding:2px 10px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);transition:background var(--dur-instant) var(--ease-out)" onmouseover="this.style.background='var(--fill-active)'" onmouseout="this.style.background='var(--control)'">--dur-instant 50ms</span>
  • <span style="display:inline-block;padding:2px 10px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);transition:background var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-out)" onmouseover="this.style.background='var(--fill-active)'" onmouseout="this.style.background='var(--control)'">--dur-fast 100ms</span>
  • <span style="display:inline-block;padding:2px 10px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);transition:background var(--dur-med) var(--ease-out)" onmouseover="this.style.background='var(--fill-active)'" onmouseout="this.style.background='var(--control)'">--dur-med 150ms</span>
  • <span style="display:inline-block;padding:2px 10px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);transition:background var(--dur-slow) var(--ease-out-quint)" onmouseover="this.style.background='var(--fill-active)'" onmouseout="this.style.background='var(--control)'">--dur-slow 200ms</span>
  • Opacity fade: <span style="opacity:var(--hover-opacity);transition:opacity var(--dur-fast) var(--ease-out)" onmouseover="this.style.opacity='1'" onmouseout="this.style.opacity='var(--hover-opacity)'">a quiet label at --hover-opacity, full on hover</span>

Usage

  • Hover is the fastest state (--dur-instant–--dur-fast) and a panel is the slowest (--dur-med–--dur-slow), because feedback under the pointer must beat the eye, while a panel's arrival can take a beat.
  • Two easings only: --ease-out for nearly everything, --ease-out-quint for the largest moves, because a third curve is a preference, not a system.
  • Only background-color, border-color, color, opacity and transform transition, because anything else animates layout and drops frames.
  • Nothing loops, nothing bounces, nothing moves on its own: motion is only ever the consequence of an input, because ambient motion steals attention from the drawing.
  • Exit may be faster than enter, never slower, because a dismissed surface should leave before the eye returns to the canvas.

Accessibility

  • prefers-reduced-motion is honoured: the shell's animation choice defaults to system (src/app.tsx), which reads the media query live and sets :root[data-animations="off"]; src/styles.css kills every transition and animation under that attribute, so states still change and nothing moves between them.
  • The behaviour under the media query is part of the browser review; the check cannot see rendered motion, and this page does not claim more than the stylesheet shows.
  • Motion here is state feedback only (a fill, a fade, a small slide); there is no parallax, no autoplay and no repeating animation to reduce.

Not tokens

  • The assistant's "turn running" dot pulse is component-local (src/assistant.css), because it is a progress indicator with its own cadence, not a chrome transition.
  • The canvas's repaint cadence is the engine's, not the chrome's, and it does not use these tokens.

Radius

Description

The corner ladder (2–5px for controls, 20px for floating surfaces, full round for pills), the one hairline width, the focus ring's stroke, and the single shadow: every box in the chrome takes its corner and stroke from these tokens. The values live in src/tokens.css; the roles are the measured Cursor 3.27.22 recipes.

Tokens

Radius

TokenValueRole
--radius-control2pxButtons and inputs: the measured control corner.
--radius-small3pxChips and small wells: one step off the control.
--radius-card4pxCards and list rows.
--radius-composer5pxThe composer's box.
--radius-elevated20pxThe glass composer, menus and popovers (Cursor §2).
--radius-pill11pxA tab or a pill-shaped chip.
--radius-round9999pxThe pill/circle radius (Chip, IconButton; Cursor §2).

Strokes and elevation

TokenValueRole
--hairline1pxThe one border width: every stroke in the chrome.
--focus-outline-w1pxThe focus ring's stroke.
--focus-outline-offset-1pxThe ring sits inside the control's box, so it never shifts the layout.
--shadowrgba(0,0,0,.45) dark / rgba(0,0,0,.18) lightThe single shadow under floating surfaces (menus, the composer).

Surface levels (which surface a floating thing sits on) are the colour tokens --chrome, --control, --panel and --surface-elevated; their ladder is on the Colors page.

Specimens

  • Radius ladder: <span style="display:inline-block;width:64px;height:24px;background:var(--control);border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:var(--radius-control);vertical-align:middle"></span> control 2 <span style="display:inline-block;width:64px;height:24px;background:var(--control);border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:var(--radius-small);vertical-align:middle"></span> small 3 <span style="display:inline-block;width:64px;height:24px;background:var(--control);border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:var(--radius-card);vertical-align:middle"></span> card 4 <span style="display:inline-block;width:64px;height:24px;background:var(--control);border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:var(--radius-composer);vertical-align:middle"></span> composer 5
  • Elevated and round: <span style="display:inline-block;width:72px;height:28px;background:var(--surface-elevated);border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:var(--radius-elevated);box-shadow:0 0 8px var(--shadow);vertical-align:middle"></span> elevated 20 <span style="display:inline-block;width:48px;height:20px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-round);vertical-align:middle"></span> round <span style="display:inline-block;width:64px;height:20px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-pill);vertical-align:middle"></span> pill 11
  • Focus ring: <span style="display:inline-block;padding:2px 10px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);outline:var(--focus-outline-w) solid var(--accent);outline-offset:var(--focus-outline-offset)">focused</span>
  • The one shadow, on --surface-elevated: <span style="display:inline-block;padding:4px 12px;background:var(--surface-elevated);border-radius:var(--radius-card);box-shadow:0 0 8px var(--shadow)">floating</span>

Usage

  • Corners are ladder steps, never eyeballed: a control is --radius-control, a chip --radius-small or --radius-round, a card --radius-card, because mixed corners read as mixed components.
  • The composer and popovers are the only 20px corners (--radius-elevated), because the large radius is what marks a floating glass surface.
  • One stroke width: every border is --hairline; a heavier stroke is a different control, not a different border, because a 2px border reads as focus.
  • The focus ring is 1px, inset (--focus-outline-offset: -1px), in --accent, because an outset ring shifts a row and an inset ring never does.
  • One shadow, one direction: floating surfaces cast --shadow; nothing else does, because a second shadow level invents a third elevation.
  • A pill shape takes --radius-round, not --radius-pill, unless the measured 11px is the point (a tab), because at small heights 11px and full-round differ by pixels nobody sees.

Accessibility

  • The focus ring is 1px in --accent, offset -1px (inset). Its contrast against every surface level is covered by the Colors page's measured grid: --accent measures 6.0:1 over --control in dark, 3.8:1 in light (above the 3:1 non-text threshold).
  • The ring is never removed without a replacement: the components' :focus-visible styles in src/ui/ui.css carry it, and the check cannot see focus behavior, so the browser review covers it.

Not tokens

  • SVG stroke widths inside icon paths are drawing values (1.5 on the 24×24 grid in src/icons.ts), not box strokes, because an icon's stroke must stay proportional to its viewBox.
  • The canvas's selection stroke width is an engine constant, not chrome, for the same reason.

Spacing

Description

One gap scale in even steps and one control-height ladder: every inset, gap and control size in the chrome is a token from these two ladders, so density stays constant across panels. The values live in src/tokens.css; the roles are the measured Cursor 3.27.22 recipes.

Tokens

Gaps and insets

TokenValueRole

--gap-33pxA chip's internal gap, a badge's inset.
--gap-44pxThe default (--gap-default): a button row, a list row's inner gap.
--gap-55pxA field's label to its input.
--gap-66pxThe composer's padding and gap (Cursor §1).
--gap-88pxA panel's inner padding, a chip row's gap.
--gap-1010pxA section's gap between blocks.
--gap-1212pxThe rail's padding, a dialog's inner gap.
--gap-1616pxThe card padding's partner: a dialog's edge inset.
--gap-defaultvar(--gap-4)The default gap: use it when no row in this table names the case.
--button-pad-x8pxA button's horizontal padding.
--button-pad-y4pxA button's vertical padding.
--field-pad-x6pxA field's horizontal padding.
--field-pad-y4pxA field's vertical padding.
--card-padding16pxA card's or panel's inner padding.

Control heights

TokenValueRole

--control-h-input24pxAn input's and an icon button's box height.

Specimens

The scale as bars, each drawn with its own token:

  • <span style="display:inline-block;width:2px;height:14px;background:var(--accent);vertical-align:middle"></span> --gap-2
  • <span style="display:inline-block;width:4px;height:14px;background:var(--accent);vertical-align:middle"></span> --gap-4
  • <span style="display:inline-block;width:8px;height:14px;background:var(--accent);vertical-align:middle"></span> --gap-8
  • <span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:14px;background:var(--accent);vertical-align:middle"></span> --gap-12
  • <span style="display:inline-block;width:16px;height:14px;background:var(--accent);vertical-align:middle"></span> --gap-16

Control ladder, each at its token height: <span style="display:inline-block;height:var(--control-h-chip);padding:0 8px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-round);vertical-align:middle">chip 20</span> <span style="display:inline-block;height:var(--control-h-row);padding:0 8px;background:var(--control);vertical-align:middle">row 22</span> <span style="display:inline-block;height:var(--control-h-input);padding:0 8px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);vertical-align:middle">input 24</span> <span style="display:inline-block;height:var(--control-h-button);padding:0 8px;background:var(--control);border-radius:var(--radius-control);vertical-align:middle">button 28</span> <span style="display:inline-block;height:var(--control-h-tab);padding:0 8px;background:var(--control);vertical-align:middle">tab 35</span>

Usage

  • Pick the step, never the pixel: a gap is one of the scale's values, because a one-off 7px is how two panels drift apart.
  • --gap-4 is the default; reach past it only when this page's table names the case, because an unnamed gap is a missing decision.
  • Insets come from the padding tokens, not the gap tokens, because a padding is part of a control's box and must survive a border change.
  • Controls stand on the height ladder (20/22/24/28/35), because two controls in one row align by their boxes, not their text.
  • Density never changes with the viewport; the canvas takes the space, because a chrome that scales steals the drawing's room.

Accessibility

  • Target sizes: the ladder's smallest box is the 20px chip; the button is 28px tall and the icon button 24px, all measured from src/tokens.css. The 24px minimum recommended by WCAG 2.5.8 is met by buttons and icon buttons; chips are not interactive targets on their own.
  • Reflow at 320px: not measured this run. The fixed 260px rail and the toolbar are the risk this review should cover first.

Not tokens

  • The canvas's own metrics (world units, line widths) are engine values, not chrome spacing; src/canvas.ts maps them, and they never appear as chrome gaps.
  • One-off optical nudges inside an icon's own SVG viewBox stay raw in src/icons.ts, because they are drawing coordinates, not layout.

Typography

Description

Two families (the system UI stack and the mono stack) and six fixed sizes, one per control and one per reading role: text never takes a size outside this scale, and sizes never scale with the viewport. The values live in src/tokens.css; the roles are fixed by the measured Cursor 3.27.22 recipes.

Tokens

TokenValueRole
--font-familysystem-ui, "Segoe UI", -apple-system, sans-serifThe interface family: labels, values, prose.
--font-family-mono"Hack", ui-monospace, "Cascadia Mono", Consolas, monospaceThe monospace family: coordinates, command input, code in messages.
--font-button14pxA button's label (src/ui/ui.css), the largest control type.
--font-chip11pxA chip, a section label, a tool tooltip.
--font-label12pxA field's label above its input.
--font-small11.5pxSecondary values: status bar readouts, units.
--font-body13pxBody copy: field values, list rows, the assistant's messages.
--font-mono12pxThe command line's input and history, coordinates.

Composite styles (family, size, line height, weight, tracking), as the app sets them:

StyleFamilySizeLine heightWeightTracking
Button label--font-family--font-button1400normal
Chip / section label--font-family--font-chip14000.05em–0.06em on uppercased section labels
Field label--font-family--font-labelnormal400normal
Body / row--font-family--font-bodynormal400normal
Assistant message--font-family--font-body1.4400normal
Command input--font-family-mono--font-mono1.45400normal

Specimens

  • Button: <span style="font-family:var(--font-family);font-size:var(--font-button)">Save</span>
  • Chip: <span style="font-family:var(--font-family);font-size:var(--font-chip)">Bodycam</span>
  • Field label: <span style="font-family:var(--font-family);font-size:var(--font-label)">Layer</span>
  • Small: <span style="font-family:var(--font-family);font-size:var(--font-small)">0,0 · 120.5 × 80</span>
  • Body: <span style="font-family:var(--font-family);font-size:var(--font-body)">Paste a command or ask the assistant.</span>
  • Mono: <span style="font-family:var(--font-family-mono);font-size:var(--font-mono)">(0,0) CIRCLE 20,20 5</span>

Usage

  • One size per role, never per surface: a button is --font-button wherever it sits, because a control that changes size between panels reads as a different control.
  • The mono family is for machine text only — coordinates, commands, code — because mixing the families inside one sentence makes both harder to scan.
  • Uppercase belongs to section labels alone, with letter-spacing at 0.05em–0.06em, because spaced caps on a normal sentence read as shouting.
  • The smallest size is --font-chip at 11px; nothing in the chrome goes below it, because below 11px the stroke font's glyphs start to blur at 100%.
  • Sizes do not scale with the viewport; the app's chrome keeps its density and the canvas handles scale, because a zoomed chrome wastes the drawing's space.

Accessibility

  • The smallest type in use is 11px (--font-chip), measured from src/tokens.css; every other role is larger, up to 14px (--font-button).
  • Body copy sits at 13px with a 1.4–1.45 line height, which the assistant pane uses for multi-line messages.
  • Zoom to 200% without clipping: not measured this run. The fixed-width chrome (a 260px rail) is the risk this review should cover first.

Not tokens

  • Font weight and line-height are set per component in src/ui/ui.css and src/styles.css, because they only matter for the roles named in the composite table above; a weight token would be a second scale for one value.
  • The mono family names Hack first, but no font file ships with the app: the stack falls through to the platform's mono when it is absent, so nothing is embedded and nothing is licensed.

Button

Description

It runs one action the moment its label says so: it never navigates and never holds a value.

import { Button } from "../../../../src/ui/Button";, source src/ui/Button.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/role-button, trap/native-control, trap/button-clone, trap/button-type, trap/control-height, trap/weight-shift, trap/button-label-wrap, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/touch-tap-highlight.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the recipe is the app's own src/ui/ui.css, measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §5), and no registry item ships it.

Variants

variant

  • primary: the one action of the pane or dialog; the accent fill. Used at 1 call site (the provider popover's Save).
  • secondary: the default action; the .08 fill that Cursor's own default button draws. Used at 0 call sites.
  • ghost: a quiet action on a tool bar or in a list; no resting fill. Used at 1 call site (the provider popover's Cancel).
  • danger: a destructive action; the error fill. Used at 0 call sites.

}

  • sm: the 24px control, for a button beside a field or inside a row. Used at 0 call sites.
  • md: the 28px default, for a dialog footer or a pane header. Used at 2 call sites (the provider popover's Cancel and Save).

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestNothing is over the button.Click it, or Tab to it.The variant's resting fill and the label.by hand
HoverThe pointer is over the button, on a device with a hover pointer.Click it.The fill steps up one rung (.08 to .14, .14 to .20); the cursor is a pointer.by hand
PressedThe pointer is held down on the button.Release to run the action.The fill takes the next rung up (.20, or the 20% mix on primary and danger).by hand

Example: A blocked action at the disabled ink and fill. (docs/system/examples/button/disabled.tsx)

import { Button } from "../../../../src/ui/Button";

export default function Disabled() {
  return <Button disabled>Save</Button>;
}

State precedence

  • Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the button; hover only steps the fill.
  • Hover and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled button keeps its resting fill under the pointer and takes no click.
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the button is held down; the fill steps up.
  • Pressed and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled button never takes the pressed fill.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-out)background-colorThe fill changes at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.
The pointer presses downinputpress (--dur-instant + --ease-out)background-colorThe fill changes at once.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
children?ElementThe label.
disabled?booleanBlocks the click, drops the label to the disabled ink and the fill to the disabled step.
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)Runs on click.
size?ButtonSizeThe control size.
title?stringA tooltip.
type?"button" | "submit" | "reset"The native type.
variant?ButtonVariantThe purpose of the action.
  • variant: the purpose of the action; the token layer picks the look. Defaults to secondary.
  • size: the control height; md is 28px and sm is 24px.
  • type: defaults to button so a button inside a form never submits by accident.
  • disabled: blocks the click and drops the ink to the disabled step.
  • title: a tooltip; it is not a substitute for the label.
  • onClick: runs on click; a disabled button never fires it.

Usage

When to use

  • The user runs one action and expects it to happen now: saving, closing, deleting, opening a dialog.
  • The action is the pane's or dialog's main one, and there is exactly one of it: the primary variant.

When not to use

  • The control is a glyph with no label. Use IconButton instead.
  • The text is a status or a value rather than an action. Use Chip instead.
  • The clickable band is a list item rather than an action. Use Row instead.

Rules

  • rule/button-variant-purpose: When a surface needs a button, pick variant by the action's purpose — 1 primary per view, secondary for the default, ghost for a quiet action, danger for a destructive one — because two accent fills in one row leave no single action and Cursor's own default button is the quiet one. Evidence: app 4/4 variants, ../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §5. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: <Button variant="primary">Cancel</Button>
  • Do: <Button>Cancel</Button>
  • rule/button-state-ladder: When a button is hovered or pressed, step the fill one rung per state — .08 to .14 on hover, .14 to .20 on press — because a fill step reads as feedback without moving the label or the box. Evidence: measured .08/.14/.20, ../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §5. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: .my-button:hover { color: var(--accent) } — a colour change instead of a fill step.
  • Do: .ui-button--secondary:hover { background: var(--fill-active) }

Content

  • rule/button-label-verb: When the label is written, use a verb the user recognizes in sentence case — Save, Delete, Zoom extents — because the label is the action's name and the accessible name comes from it. Evidence: single use src/components/TopBar.tsx:47, the label "Zoom extents". Check: review src/components/TopBar.tsx.
  • Don't: <Button>SAVE</Button>
  • Do: <Button>Save</Button>

Anti-slop

  • rule/button-canonical-element: When a surface needs a button, render Button rather than a raw <button> with its own class, because the replaced classes paint 6 different hover fills and 3 different radii by hand. Evidence: app 22/22 lines across assistant.css and AssistantPane.tsx, rg -c "assistant-send|assistant-save|assistant-ghost|assistant-preset" src. Check: review src/ui/Button.tsx.
  • Don't: <button class="assistant-ghost" onClick={save}>Save</button>
  • Do: <Button variant="ghost" onClick={save}>Save</Button>

Limits

  • rule/button-row-limit: When one row or dialog footer holds more than 3 buttons, move the rest into a menu, because the measured composer toolbar holds 3 actions at 24px each and a fourth starts competing with the input. Evidence: measured 3 actions at 24px, ../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §2. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: 5 buttons side by side in the pane's toolbar row.
  • Do: 2 buttons in the row and the rest inside a menu.

Accessibility

Rests on the native <button> element: role, Enter and Space, disabled, and form behaviour come from the platform.

Related

  • IconButton: when the action is one glyph with a tooltip and no label.
  • Row: when the clickable band is a list item rather than an action.
  • Chip: when the text is a fact or a value, not an action.
  • Field: when the control holds an editable value rather than performing an action.
  • SectionLabel: when the text names a group rather than performing an action.

Chip

Description

It shows one compact fact, a keyword or a suggestion, and it only acts when the caller gives it a handler.

import { Chip } from "../../../../src/ui/Chip";, source src/ui/Chip.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/role-button, trap/native-control, trap/control-height, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded, trap/touch-tap-highlight.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the pill radius, the 20px height and the accent tint are measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §2 and §5), and no registry item ships it.

Examples

<Chip>26 objects</Chip> — the selection count as a static fact.

Real uses, 0 call sites (rg -c "keyword-chip" src → src/components/CommandLine.tsx:1, src/interaction.css:3):

  • (planned) src/components/CommandLine.tsx:99 — <button class="keyword-chip"> for each command keyword moves onto <Chip tone="accent" onClick={...}> when the surface migration reaches the command line.

    </div>

Variants

tone

  • neutral: a quiet fact or a value; transparent, at the faint ink. Used at 0 call sites.
  • accent: a keyword or a suggestion the user can pick; the accent-tinted fill. Used at 0 call sites.

}

Example: The accent-tinted keyword. (docs/system/examples/chip/tone-accent.tsx)

}

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
StaticThe caller passes no handler.Read it. It is a <span>: no tab stop, no pointer.The pill's text; no cursor change.test
RestThe caller passes onClick.Click it, or Tab to it.The pill is a <button>; the cursor is a pointer.test
HoverThe pointer is over the interactive chip, on a device with a hover pointer.Click it.The .08 fill.by hand
PressedThe pointer is held down.Release to run the handler.The .14 fill.by hand
FocusedKeyboard focus arrives by Tab.Enter or Space runs the handler.The 1px accent ring at offset -1, following the pill.by hand

State precedence

  • Static and Hover: Not applicable: a static chip is a <span> and takes no pointer or hover styles.
  • Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the chip; hover only adds the fill.
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the chip is held down.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters or leaves an interactive chipinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-out)background-colorThe fill changes at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
children?ElementThe chip's text.
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)When present the chip is interactive and renders as a <button>; without it, a <span>.
title?stringA tooltip; on the interactive form it is also the accessible name when the text is short.
tone?ChipToneThe tone.
  • tone: neutral or accent; defaults to neutral.
  • onClick: when present the chip renders as a <button>; without it, as a <span>.
  • title: a tooltip; on the interactive form the text is the accessible name.
  • children: the chip's text: a noun or a short value, never a sentence.

Usage

When to use

  • A value or a status needs a compact, non-editable shape: the selection count, the current units, a keyword.
  • A list of keywords or suggestions can be picked one at a time, and each pick runs an action.

When not to use

  • The user runs an action that needs a label. Use Button instead.
  • The control is a glyph with a tooltip. Use IconButton instead.
  • The value is editable. Use Field instead.

Rules

  • rule/chip-interactive-only-with-handler: When a chip runs an action, pass onClick so it renders as a <button>; when it is a fact, pass nothing so it stays a <span>, because a fact in the tab order adds a stop that does nothing. Evidence: app 2/2 chip surfaces — 1 interactive and 1 static — src/components/CommandLine.tsx:99 and src/components/TopBar.tsx:30. Check: test src/ui/Chip.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Chip>26 objects</Chip> inside an onClick wrapper div.
  • Do: <Chip onClick={() => pick("line")}>line</Chip>
  • rule/chip-tone-meaning: When a chip's tone is picked, use accent only for a keyword the user can pick and neutral for a value, because the accent tint is the app's signal for the accent role and 2 tinted chips in one row read as 2 selections. Evidence: app 2/2 chips, accent only on the keyword row, src/components/CommandLine.tsx:99. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: <Chip tone="accent">26 objects</Chip>
  • Do: <Chip>26 objects</Chip>

Content

  • rule/chip-text-short: When a chip's text is written, keep it to 1 word or a number plus its unit (26 objects, line, mm), because the pill is 20px tall and a third word starts wrapping the row. Evidence: single use src/components/CommandLine.tsx:99, the label "line". Check: review src/components/CommandLine.tsx.
  • Don't: <Chip>The current drawing has 26 objects</Chip>
  • Do: <Chip>26 objects</Chip>

Anti-slop

  • rule/chip-canonical-element: When a surface needs a chip, render Chip rather than a styled <span> or <button> with its own pill, because the replaced class hard-codes its own radius and hover and skips the static/interactive split. Evidence: app 4/4 lines in src/interaction.css, rg -c "keyword-chip" src. Check: review src/ui/Chip.tsx.
  • Don't: <span class="keyword-chip">line</span> with a click handler on the row.
  • Do: <Chip tone="accent" onClick={() => pick("line")}>line</Chip>

Limits

  • rule/chip-row-limit: When a chip row holds more than 6 chips, wrap the row or move the rest behind a "More" chip, because the measured chip is 20px tall with 8px side padding and a 608px composer row fits 6 of them before the row wraps. Evidence: measured 20px chip and 608px composer, ../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §2. Check: review src/components/CommandLine.tsx.
  • Don't: 9 chips in one unwrapped row.
  • Do: 6 chips and a "More" chip that opens the rest.

Accessibility

Rests on the native element each form renders: a <span> for the static chip, a <button> for the interactive one.

Field

Description

It takes one line of text and hands every keystroke back to the caller, who owns the value.

import { Field } from "../../../../src/ui/Field";, source src/ui/Field.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/native-control, trap/control-height, trap/field-label, trap/field-input-type, trap/touch-input-zoom, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the 24px height, the hairline stroke and the focus border are measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §5), and no registry item ships it.

Examples

<Field value={name} ariaLabel="Layer name" onInput={setName} /> — the layer name, owned by the panel.

  • (planned) src/components/CommandLine.tsx — class="cmd-input" (1 use) moves onto <Field type="search"> in the command line.

State precedence

  • Focused and Hover: Focused wins. The accent stroke and the ring stay while the pointer is over the field.
  • Filled and Focused: both show. The accent stroke and ring draw over the filled value.
  • Disabled and Hover: Disabled wins. A disabled field takes no hover and no ring.
  • Disabled and Filled: Disabled wins. The value stays visible at the disabled ink.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
Focus arrives or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-out)border-colorThe stroke changes at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
ariaLabel?stringThe accessible name when no visible <label> is tied to the input.
autoFocus?booleanFocus the input when it mounts.
disabled?booleanBlocks typing and drops the ink to the disabled step.
onInput?((value: string) => void)Runs on every keystroke with the new value.
placeholder?stringThe placeholder.
title?stringA tooltip.
type?"text" | "email" | "search" | "password"The native input type.
value?stringThe current value.
  • value: the current value; the caller holds it and passes the new one back.
  • onInput: runs on every keystroke with the new value.
  • placeholder: the hint; never the only name.
  • ariaLabel: the accessible name when no visible label is tied to the input.
  • type: the native input type; defaults to text.
  • disabled: blocks typing and drops the ink to the disabled step.
  • title: a tooltip.
  • autoFocus: focuses the field when it mounts.

Usage

When to use

  • The user types or edits 1 line of text: a name, a coordinate, a keyword.
  • The value is owned by a surface above the field, which needs every keystroke.

When not to use

  • The value is picked from a set rather than typed. Use Chip instead.
  • The control is an action rather than a value. Use Button instead.
  • The text is a fact to read. Use Chip instead.

Rules

  • rule/field-label-bound: When a field is rendered without a visible <label>, pass ariaLabel, because a placeholder disappears as soon as the user types and the field is left nameless. Evidence: app 3/3 single-line inputs are named by their row, rg -c "assistant-input|cmd-input|prop-input" src. Check: test src/ui/Field.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Field placeholder="Layer name" /> alone in a row.
  • Do: <Field ariaLabel="Layer name" placeholder="Layer name" />
  • rule/field-type-native: When a field takes an email, a search term or a password, pass type so the native keyboard and autofill follow, because type="text" on an email field shows the wrong phone keyboard and blocks autofill. Evidence: app 4/4 types defined in src/ui/Field.tsx. Check: test src/ui/Field.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Field type="text" ariaLabel="Email" />
  • Do: <Field type="email" ariaLabel="Email" />

Content

  • rule/field-placeholder-example: When a placeholder is written, show a real example value rather than an instruction (0,0 — not "Enter a point"), because the placeholder is read as the value's shape, and the instruction belongs in a label. Evidence: single use src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:152, the value-style placeholder. Check: review src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <Field placeholder="Type your point here" />
  • Do: <Field ariaLabel="Base point" placeholder="0,0" />

Anti-slop

  • rule/field-canonical-element: When a surface needs a single-line input, render Field rather than a raw <input> with its own class, because the replaced classes paint 3 different heights and borders by hand. Evidence: app 9/9 lines across src/styles.css, src/interaction.css and src/assistant.css, rg -c "assistant-input|cmd-input|prop-input" src. Check: review src/ui/Field.tsx.
  • Don't: <input class="prop-input" value={x} onInput={...} />
  • Do: <Field value={x} onInput={setX} ariaLabel="Name" />

Limits

  • rule/field-width-limit: When a field sits in a form row beside other controls, give it at least 96px or let it fill the row, because the measured palette input is 6px-padded inside a 260px sidebar and a narrower field clips a 4-character value like "0,0". Evidence: measured 6px padding and 260px sidebar, ../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §3. Check: review src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: a 40px-wide field in the properties row.
  • Do: a field that fills the row's remaining width.

Accessibility

Rests on the native <input> element: typing, selection, IME and autofill come from the platform.

IconButton

Description

It runs one action drawn as a single glyph, and its tooltip is its accessible name.

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the circle, the .08 hover fill and the 14px glyph are measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §2), and the glyphs are the app's own src/icons.ts paths.

  • ghost: the transparent circle for a tool bar; the default. Used at 0 call sites.
  • soft: the resting .08 fill, for a tool that is currently on. Used at 1 call site (the composer's attach).
  • inverted: the ink-coloured circle with the accent-surface glyph, for the one primary action. Used at 2 call sites (the composer's stop and send).

Example: The transparent circle with the .08 hover fill. (docs/system/examples/icon-button/variant-ghost.tsx)

import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";

export default function VariantGhost() {
  return <IconButton icon="attach" title="Attach files" variant="ghost" />;
}

Example: The resting .08 fill, for a tool that is on. (docs/system/examples/icon-button/variant-soft.tsx)

import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";

export default function VariantSoft() {
  return <IconButton icon="list" title="List view" variant="soft" selected />;
}

Example: The white circle: the composer's send. (docs/system/examples/icon-button/variant-inverted.tsx)

import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";

export default function VariantInverted() {
  return <IconButton icon="send" title="Send" variant="inverted" />;
}

size

  • sm: the 20px circle with the 12px glyph, for a chip row. Used at 1 call site (an attachment chip's remove).
  • md: the 24px circle with the 14px glyph, the composer's size. Used at 3 call sites (the composer's attach, stop and send).

Example: The 20px circle with the 12px glyph. (docs/system/examples/icon-button/size-sm.tsx)

import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";

export default function SizeSm() {
  return <IconButton icon="close" title="Close" size="sm" />;
}

Example: The 24px circle with the 14px glyph. (docs/system/examples/icon-button/size-md.tsx)

import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";

export default function SizeMd() {
  return <IconButton icon="close" title="Close" size="md" />;
}

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestNothing is over the circle.Click it, or Tab to it.The variant's resting fill, or none on ghost.by hand
HoverThe pointer is over the circle, on a device with a hover pointer.Click it.The fill steps up one rung; the cursor is a pointer.by hand
PressedThe pointer is held down.Release to run the action.The next fill rung up.by hand
FocusedKeyboard focus arrives by Tab.Enter or Space runs the action.The 1px accent ring at offset -1, following the circle.by hand
SelectedThe caller passes selected (a toggle).Click it again to turn the tool off.The .14 fill, the full ink, and aria-pressed="true".test
DisabledThe caller's condition is false.Nothing: no click, no hover.The glyph drops to the disabled ink; the fill to the disabled step.test

Example: A blocked tool at the disabled ink. (docs/system/examples/icon-button/disabled.tsx)

import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";

export default function Disabled() {
  return <IconButton icon="stop" title="Stop" disabled />;
}

Example: A toggled tool at the .14 fill, announced pressed. (docs/system/examples/icon-button/selected.tsx)

import { IconButton } from "../../../../src/ui/IconButton";

export default function Selected() {
  return <IconButton icon="list" title="List view" selected />;
}

State precedence

  • Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the circle; hover only steps the fill.
  • Hover and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled circle keeps its resting look under the pointer and takes no click.
  • Selected and Hover: both show. The .14 selected fill stays; hover adds the pointer cursor and takes the fill to the pressed rung on press.
  • Selected and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled toggle drops to the disabled ink and takes no click.
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the circle is held down.

Motion

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion
The pointer enters or leavesinputhover / focus feedback (--dur-fast + --ease-out)background-color, colorThe fill and the ink change at once: the shell's :root[data-animations="off"] * rule removes the transition.
The pointer presses downinputpress (--dur-instant + --ease-out)background-colorThe fill changes at once.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
iconstringThe id from ../icons.ts; the glyph is drawn in code.
titlestringThe accessible name (also aria-label), and the tooltip.
disabled?booleanBlocks the click and drops the glyph to the disabled ink.
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)Runs on click.
selected?booleanA toggle-style icon button: sets aria-pressed and the .14 selected fill.
size?IconButtonSizeThe box size.
variant?IconButtonVariantThe look.
  • icon: the id from src/icons.ts; the glyph is drawn in code, never an image.
  • title: the accessible name and the tooltip; an icon alone has no name without it.
  • variant: the look; defaults to ghost.
  • size: the circle; md is 24px with a 14px glyph, sm is 20px with a 12px glyph.
  • selected: sets aria-pressed and the .14 selected fill.
  • disabled: blocks the click and drops the glyph to the disabled ink.
  • onClick: runs on click; a disabled circle never fires it.

Usage

When to use

  • The action is one glyph a tooltip can name: close, attach, send, stop, add.
  • The control sits in a tool bar, a panel header or a toolbar row where a label would crowd the row.

When not to use

  • The action needs a label to be understood. Use Button instead.
  • The control is a list item with a name. Use Row instead.
  • The glyph is a status rather than an action. Use Chip instead.

Rules

  • rule/icon-button-name: When an icon button is rendered, pass title for every use, because the glyph alone leaves the accessible name empty and a screen reader announces "button". Evidence: app 3/3 composer icon buttons, src/components/AssistantPane.tsx. Check: test src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <IconButton icon="close" /> — no name.
  • Do: <IconButton icon="close" title="Close the panel" />
  • rule/icon-button-one-inverted: When a toolbar row holds icon buttons, keep at most 1 inverted circle, because the ink-coloured circle is the row's primary action and a second one splits the eye. Evidence: measured 1 inverted send button in the composer toolbar, ../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §2. Check: review src/ui/ui.css.
  • Don't: two variant="inverted" circles in the composer row.
  • Do: 1 inverted send and ghost for attach and stop.

Content

  • rule/icon-button-title-sentence: When title is written, name the action in sentence case with no full stop (Close the panel, Send, Stop), because the same string is the tooltip and the accessible name. Evidence: single use src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:454, the "Attach a picture (or paste, or drop one)" label. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: title="close panel."
  • Do: title="Close the panel"

Anti-slop

  • rule/icon-button-canonical-element: When a surface needs an icon action, render IconButton rather than a raw <button> with a hand-sized glyph, because the replaced classes hard-code 3 different box sizes and their own hover opacities. Evidence: app 10/10 lines across src/assistant.css and src/components/AssistantPane.tsx, rg -c "assistant-icon|assistant-attachment-x" src. Check: review src/ui/IconButton.tsx.
  • Don't: <button class="assistant-icon" onClick={stop}>…</button>
  • Do: <IconButton icon="stop" title="Stop" onClick={stop} />

Limits

  • rule/icon-button-row-limit: When a toolbar row holds more than 5 icon buttons, move the rest into a menu, because the measured composer row holds 3 at 24px each with 4px gaps and the row starts crowding the input past 5. Evidence: measured 3 actions at 24px with 4px gaps, ../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §2. Check: review src/components/AssistantPane.tsx.
  • Don't: 6 circles in the composer's toolbar row.
  • Do: 3 circles in the row and the rest inside a menu.

Accessibility

Rests on the native <button> element, with the drawn glyph hidden from assistive tech.

Row

Description

It is the full-width clickable band of a list: a menu item, a property row or a layer, marked current when it is the selected one.

import { Row } from "../../../../src/ui/Row";, source src/ui/Row.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/button-div, trap/role-button, trap/native-control, trap/list-dead-gap, trap/current-unmarked, trap/menu-navigation, trap/control-height, trap/focus-ring-shape, trap/hover-beats-focus, trap/disabled-still-hovers, trap/touch-hover-flash, trap/hover-unguarded.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the 22px row, the 4px inset and the .14 selected fill are measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §3 and §5), and no registry item ships it.

Examples

<Row onClick={pick}>Layer 1</Row> — one layer in the layers list.

Real uses, 1 call site (rg -c "<Row" src/components → src/components/AssistantPane.tsx:1, the provider popover's preset list):

  • src/components/AssistantPane.tsx — the composer pilot: the provider popover's preset rows; the transcript's tool rows and the composer's toolbar row stay bespoke (the toolbar is a container, and the tool row carries a disclosure arrow and a note).
  • (planned) src/components/MenuBar.tsx — .menu-row (1 use) moves onto <Row> when the surface migration reaches the menus.
  • (planned) src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:167 — .prop-row (1 use) moves onto <Row> when the properties palette is migrated.
  • .layer-row (LayersPanel) stays bespoke because its row nests a toggle cluster, and a button cannot nest buttons.

Variants

Not applicable

Not applicable: no variant axes — a row is one band; the selected and disabled props are states, and its height, padding and ink come from the one recipe.

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestNothing is over the row.Click it, or Tab to it.The label at the dim ink; the full width is the hit area.test
HoverThe pointer is over the row, on a device with a hover pointer.Click it.The .08 fill; the cursor is a pointer.by hand
PressedThe pointer is held down.Release to run the action.Nothing beyond hover: a row's press runs on release.by hand
FocusedKeyboard focus arrives by Tab.Enter or Space runs the action.The 1px accent ring at offset -1, following the 4px radius.by hand

export default function Disabled() {
  return <Row disabled>Locked layer</Row>;
}

State precedence

  • Hover and Selected: Selected wins. The .14 selected fill stays under the pointer; hover adds nothing to the fill.
  • Hover and Focused: Focused wins. The ring stays drawn while the pointer is over the row.
  • Hover and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled row keeps its resting look and takes no click.
  • Selected and Disabled: Disabled wins. A disabled row drops the selected fill and shows the disabled ink.
  • Pressed and Focused: both show. The ring stays drawn while the row is held down.

TriggerKindPresetPropertiesReduced motion

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
children?ElementThe row's content: a label, and quiet trailing text such as a shortcut or a value.
disabled?booleanBlocks the click and drops the ink to the disabled step.
onClick?((event: MouseEvent) => void)Runs on click.
selected?booleanThe current row: the .14 fill, the full ink, and aria-current="true".
title?stringA tooltip.
  • selected: the current row; sets aria-current="true" and the .14 fill.
  • disabled: blocks the click and drops the ink to the disabled step.
  • title: a tooltip, for a row whose label is clipped.
  • onClick: runs on click; a disabled row never fires it.
  • children: the row's content: a label, and quiet trailing text such as a shortcut.

Usage

When to use

  • One item of a list is clickable and runs one action: a menu item, a layer, a property.
  • The current item of that list must be marked for a screen reader as well as the eye.

When not to use

  • The action is a single control with a label. Use Button instead.
  • The row nests its own controls (a toggle cluster, a stepper). Use Button and IconButton in a bespoke band instead, because a button cannot nest buttons.
  • The band is a heading above a list rather than a row in it. Use SectionLabel instead.

Rules

  • rule/row-one-action: When a row runs an action, wire it on Row itself rather than on a label inside it, because a label-only hit area leaves dead space that reads as broken. Evidence: app 8/8 lines across src/chrome.css, src/components/MenuBar.tsx and src/styles.css, rg -c "menu-row" src. Check: test src/ui/Row.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <Row><span onClick={pick}>Layer 1</span></Row>
  • Do: <Row onClick={pick}>Layer 1</Row>
  • rule/row-current-marked: When a list has a current item, pass selected on it, because the .14 fill alone is colour and a screen reader needs aria-current="true" to hear it. Evidence: app 3/3 list surfaces draw a current row, src/styles.css. Check: test src/ui/Row.test.tsx.
  • Don't: a hand-painted background on the current row with no aria-current.
  • Do: <Row selected>Current layer</Row>

Content

  • rule/row-trailing-quiet: When a row carries a shortcut or a value, put it after the label in the dim ink (--text-faint), because the label is what the user scans and the trailing text is secondary. Evidence: single use src/components/MenuBar.tsx:174, the shortcut span. Check: review src/components/MenuBar.tsx.
  • Don't: a shortcut before the label.
  • Do: <Row>Save<span class="row-shortcut">Ctrl+S</span></Row>

Anti-slop

  • rule/row-canonical-element: When a surface needs a list band, render Row rather than a div with an onClick, because a div has no role, no focus and no disabled state, and the replaced classes repeat hover and selected by hand. Evidence: app 23/23 lines across 7 files, rg -c "prop-row|menu-row|assistant-row|assistant-tool" src. Check: review src/ui/Row.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="menu-row" onClick={pick}>Open</div>
  • Do: <Row onClick={pick}>Open</Row>

Limits

  • rule/row-label-limit: When a row's label runs past 40 characters at the 260px sidebar, clip it with an ellipsis and keep the full text in title, because the measured row is 22px tall and the sidebar 260px wide. Evidence: measured 22px row and 260px sidebar, ../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §3. Check: review src/styles.css.
  • Don't: a 60-character layer name that overflows the row.
  • Do: a clipped label with the full name in title.

Accessibility

Rests on the native <button> element: role, Enter and Space, disabled and focus come from the platform.

SectionLabel

Description

It names a panel's section as a real heading, so a screen reader can jump between the sections by heading.

import { SectionLabel } from "../../../../src/ui/SectionLabel";, source src/ui/SectionLabel.tsx, status ready. Foundation: hand-rolled. Traps checked: trap/native-control.

Foundation

Not applicable: hand-rolled — the 11px uppercase header is measured from the running Cursor 3.27.22 (../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §3), and no registry item ships it.

Examples

<SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel> — the heading above the layers list.

Real uses, 0 call sites (rg -c "section-label" src/components src/styles.css → src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:1, src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx:1, src/styles.css:1):

  • (planned) src/components/LayersPanel.tsx and src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx — .section-label (2 uses) move onto <SectionLabel> when the surface migration reaches the panels.

Not applicable

Not applicable: no variant axes — a section label is one heading; its size, weight and ink come from the one recipe, and anything that looks different is a different role (a pane title, a tab).

States

StateTriggerWhat the user can doShown by, besides colorChecked by
RestThe heading is rendered.Read it; jump to it by heading navigation.The uppercase label at the faint ink.test

State precedence

  • Rest and Long label: Not applicable: the heading has no other state; a long label is the same resting state with more text.

Motion

Not applicable: no motion — the heading never changes state, and its ink comes from the tokens.

Props

PropTypeDefaultPurpose
children?ElementThe section's name.
  • children: the section's name: one or two words, the same noun the panel uses elsewhere.

Usage

When to use

  • A panel or a popover holds more than one group, and each group needs a name a screen reader can jump to.
  • The name sits above a list, a table or a group of controls as their heading.

When not to use

  • The text is an action rather than a name. Use Button instead.
  • The text is a value or a status. Use Chip instead.
  • The text is a list item the user can pick. Use Row instead.

Rules

  • rule/section-label-heading-element: When a section label is rendered, keep it an <h2>, because the element is what lets a screen reader jump between panels and a styled <div> reads as plain text. Evidence: app 3/3 panels draw a section header, src/components/LayersPanel.tsx. Check: test src/ui/SectionLabel.test.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="section-label">Layers</div>
  • Do: <SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel>
  • rule/section-label-not-action: When a heading needs a control beside it, put the control outside SectionLabel rather than inside it, because a button inside a heading joins the heading's name and garbles heading navigation. Evidence: app 2/2 panel heads keep their controls in the bar, src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx. Check: review src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <SectionLabel>Layers <IconButton icon="plus" title="New layer" /></SectionLabel>
  • Do: <div class="head"><SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel><IconButton icon="plus" title="New layer" /></div>

Content

  • rule/section-label-one-noun: When the label's text is written, use 1 noun in title case (Layers, Properties, Selection), because the label is uppercased by CSS and a sentence reads as shouting. Evidence: single use src/components/LayersPanel.tsx:25, the label "Layers". Check: review src/components/LayersPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <SectionLabel>Here are your layers</SectionLabel>
  • Do: <SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel>

Anti-slop

  • rule/section-label-canonical-element: When a surface needs a section header, render SectionLabel rather than a styled <div> or a bespoke class, because the replaced class is a bare rule with no role and drifts per panel. Evidence: app 3/3 lines across 2 panels and src/styles.css, rg -c "section-label" src/components src/styles.css. Check: review src/ui/SectionLabel.tsx.
  • Don't: <div class="section-label">Properties</div>
  • Do: <SectionLabel>Properties</SectionLabel>

Limits

  • rule/section-label-word-limit: When a section's name runs past 2 words, shorten it to 1 or 2 words, because the measured header row is 22px at 11px type and a third word starts clipping in a 260px sidebar. Evidence: measured 22px header at 11px type, ../../../../../.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md §3. Check: review src/components/LayersPanel.tsx.
  • Don't: <SectionLabel>Layer visibility and lock state</SectionLabel>
  • Do: <SectionLabel>Layers</SectionLabel>

Accessibility

Rests on the native <h2> element: heading role and level come from the platform, and heading navigation works without ARIA.

rule/chip-text-shortWhen a chip's text is written, keep it to 1 word or a number plus its unit (26 objects, line, mm), because the pill is 20px tall and a third word starts wrapping the row.components/chipsingle usereview src/components/CommandLine.tsx
rule/chip-tone-meaningWhen a chip's tone is picked, use accent only for a keyword the user can pick and neutral for a value, because the accent tint is the app's signal for the accent role and 2 tinted chips in one row read as 2 selections.components/chipappreview src/ui/ui.css

rule/deprecated-importAn import of a component the registry says was replacednone yetscripts/check-system.mjs
rule/doubled-utilityA Tailwind v4 utility that repeats its property word, such as text-text-muted, bg-bg-subtle or border-border-strong. It comes from a --color-<role> token whose role starts with text, bg or bordernone yetscripts/check-system.mjs
rule/field-canonical-elementWhen a surface needs a single-line input, render Field rather than a raw <input> with its own class, because the replaced classes paint 3 different heights and borders by hand.components/fieldappreview src/ui/Field.tsx
rule/field-label-boundWhen a field is rendered without a visible <label>, pass ariaLabel, because a placeholder disappears as soon as the user types and the field is left nameless.components/fieldapptest src/ui/Field.test.tsx
rule/field-placeholder-exampleWhen a placeholder is written, show a real example value rather than an instruction (0,0 — not "Enter a point"), because the placeholder is read as the value's shape, and the instruction belongs in a label.components/fieldsingle usereview src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx
rule/field-type-nativeWhen a field takes an email, a search term or a password, pass type so the native keyboard and autofill follow, because type="text" on an email field shows the wrong phone keyboard and blocks autofill.components/fieldapptest src/ui/Field.test.tsx
rule/field-width-limitWhen a field sits in a form row beside other controls, give it at least 96px or let it fill the row, because the measured palette input is 6px-padded inside a 260px sidebar and a narrower field clips a 4-character value like "0,0".components/fieldmeasuredreview src/components/PropertiesPanel.tsx
rule/icon-button-canonical-elementWhen a surface needs an icon action, render IconButton rather than a raw <button> with a hand-sized glyph, because the replaced classes hard-code 3 different box sizes and their own hover opacities.components/icon-buttonappreview src/ui/IconButton.tsx
rule/icon-button-nameWhen an icon button is rendered, pass title for every use, because the glyph alone leaves the accessible name empty and a screen reader announces "button".components/icon-buttonapptest src/ui/IconButton.test.tsx
rule/icon-button-one-invertedWhen a toolbar row holds icon buttons, keep at most 1 inverted circle, because the ink-coloured circle is the row's primary action and a second one splits the eye.components/icon-buttonmeasuredreview src/ui/ui.css
rule/icon-button-row-limitWhen a toolbar row holds more than 5 icon buttons, move the rest into a menu, because the measured composer row holds 3 at 24px each with 4px gaps and the row starts crowding the input past 5.components/icon-buttonmeasuredreview src/components/AssistantPane.tsx

rule/raw-valueHex, rgb(), hsl() or oklch() outside a token source line, including inside Tailwind arbitrary valuesnone yetscripts/check-system.mjs
rule/row-canonical-elementWhen a surface needs a list band, render Row rather than a div with an onClick, because a div has no role, no focus and no disabled state, and the replaced classes repeat hover and selected by hand.components/rowappreview src/ui/Row.tsx

What the check can't see

A reviewer or a browser covers these. Passing cd apps/ui && bun run check says nothing about them.

  • Rendered contrast, including non-text contrast of borders, focus rings and checkbox edges. Measure it in a browser.
  • Behavior: what a click, Enter or Escape does, focus order and focus return, and whether Cancel submits.
  • Layout at each viewport, overflow at 390px and touch target sizes.
  • Visual overrides on components the registry does not list, and overrides built at runtime: cn() branches, spread props, a class name held in a variable.
  • A loading state shown some other way than a label ternary on the button, such as a label read from a variable.
  • Class names and values built at runtime, such as template strings, cn() branches or fontSize: size / 2.5.
  • bg-white and text-black when the theme defines no role for their job, their opacity forms such as bg-black/50, and CSS keywords such as white in var() fallbacks.
  • Files outside the include folders, and ui files missing from the drift list (they are scanned, but no hash guards them).
  • Whether a token's role comment still matches how the token is used.
  • Rules the generated rules page marks review, or enforces only through their own Check: clause.
  • Motion that is only measured: exit slower than enter, frequent-surface motion, linear easing, press delay, input lag and jank. Easing set in script or through a variable, and hover reveals written as Tailwind classes (v4 guards hover: itself, v3 does not).
  • Whether a pressed style covers the control whose tap highlight was removed: any pressed style in the repo passes trap/touch-tap-highlight.

The web system's design decisions

The lock for the SolidJS UI (apps/ui), taken in the design-system run of 2026-10-28. The design source is the running Cursor 3.27.22 desktop app, measured live (.design-system/research/cursor-recipes-2026-10-28.md). The values live in src/tokens.css; this file records the picks and the reasons, so the next surface does not re-litigate them.

Canonical picks

The web UI grows six canonical components under src/ui/, each a thin wrapper over the native element. The per-surface hand-rolled classes they replace are named below; a class loses because it is a one-off with no shared API and no states.

  • Button — pick ui/Button.tsx (native <button>). Variants primary | secondary | ghost | danger, default secondary (Cursor's own default button). Loses: .button (TopBar — one call site), .assistant-send / .assistant-save / .assistant-ghost (assistant-only, their own colours), .assistant-preset (a suggestion chip wearing a button), .tool-button (ToolStrip — a grid cell, no variants), .menu-row (a menu item, not a general button).
  • IconButton — pick ui/IconButton.tsx (native <button>, a drawn icon + label). Variants ghost | soft | inverted; sizes md (24px) and sm (20px). Loses: .assistant-icon (three uses, fixed 24px, no variant), .assistant-attachment-x (one-off), .layer-toggles buttons (LayersPanel — a toggle cluster with its own semantics), .status-toggle (StatusBar — tab-ish, keeps role="tab").
  • Chip — pick ui/Chip.tsx (native <button> when interactive, <span> when not). Loses: .chip (TopBar — a static fact, no interaction), .keyword-chip (CommandLine — interactive, no tone/size API), .cmd-chips (a container, not a chip).
  • Field — pick ui/Field.tsx (native <input>, single-line). Loses: .assistant-input, .cmd-input, .prop-input (each one surface's own padding and border), .assistant-field (a label wrapper, not the control). The composer's auto-growing <textarea> and the properties palette's <select> stay bespoke for now (found-not-fixed).
  • Row — pick ui/Row.tsx (native <button>, the full-width clickable band). Loses: .prop-row, .menu-row, .assistant-row, .assistant-tool (each repeats hover/selected padding by hand). A grid row carrying nested controls of its own (.layer-row with its toggle cluster) stays bespoke — a button cannot nest buttons.
  • SectionLabel — pick ui/SectionLabel.tsx (native <h2> — a heading, so a screen reader can jump between panels). Loses: .section-label (already shared but untyped — the pick is its typed home), .properties-head / .layers-head (the surrounding bar, not the label), .assistant-title (a pane title, a different role).

Prop vocabulary

  • variant: primary | secondary | ghost | danger (default secondary) — purpose, not appearance.
  • size: sm | md (default md).
  • plus disabled, selected, title.
  • Chip tone: neutral | accent.
  • No boolean style props (round, big, blue): a prop names a purpose; the token layer picks the look.

Motion presets

One job, one preset (durations and easings from tokens.css):

  • press → --dur-instant + --ease-out.
  • hover / focus feedback → --dur-fast + --ease-out.
  • open (menu, popover, composer focus) → --dur-med + --ease-out-quint.
  • close → --dur-fast + --ease-out.
  • panel / larger change → --dur-slow + --ease-out.
  • Reduced motion: the app's data-animations attribute already gates motion; the presets keep it — no preset plays when animations are off.

Icon sizes

  • 14px glyph in a 24px control — icon buttons.
  • 16px glyph in a 28px control — tool strip / buttons.
  • 12px glyph in a 20px control — chips.
  • Icons stay code-drawn (src/icons.ts); no new icon assets (project rule: no third-party iconography).

What follows the drawing

Tokens left untouched because they describe the document, not the chrome: --canvas, --grid-minor, --grid-major, --axis-x, --axis-y, --crosshair, --paper, --grip-hot, --layer-current, --icon-layer-*, --icon-locked, --icon-current, --icon-point, --swatch-border, --control, --control-hover, --cmd-bg, --cmd-border, --cmd-history, --shadow, and the dark --snap / --warn / --error / --toggle-on (already Cursor's, §1). Geometry that was not re-measured also stays: --dur-med, --ease-out, all other radii, all gaps, control heights, fonts. src/canvas.ts reads the model-space colours from the CSS custom properties at runtime, so the drawing and the chrome cannot drift.
